artists.biography: Clutch is an American rock band from Germantown, Maryland. Since its formation in 1991, the band line-up has included Tim Sult (lead guitar), Dan Maines (bass), Jean-Paul Gaster (drums), and Neil Fallon (vocals, rhythm guitar, keyboards). To date, Clutch has released thirteen studio albums, and several rarities and live albums. Since 2008, the band has been signed to their own record label, Weathermaker Music.

perplexity.description:
Released on March 15, 2013 by Weathermaker Music, Earth Rocker is the tenth studio album by American rock band Clutch. The album marks a return to a more energetic and streamlined sound, blending the band’s signature stoner rock and hard rock elements with a renewed sense of urgency and groove. Produced by Machine, who also helmed their acclaimed 2004 album Blast Tyrant, Earth Rocker features 11 tracks that showcase Clutch’s trademark crunch, Neil Fallon’s dynamic vocals, and a mix of high-octane riffs and controlled aggression. Songs like the title track “Earth Rocker,” “Crucial Velocity,” and “Gone Cold” highlight the band’s ability to balance relentless energy with moments of dynamic contrast.

Earth Rocker stands as a pivotal release in Clutch’s discography, coming after a four-year gap since their previous album, Strange Cousins from the West (2009). The band consciously refined their songwriting process, completing songs before entering the studio rather than relying on improvisation, which contributed to the album’s tight, focused feel. Critics praised the album for merging Clutch’s classic sound with a fresh, revitalized approach, noting its confident performances and effective blend of past influences with new ideas. The album’s success helped set the stage for the band’s subsequent commercial breakthrough with Psychic Warfare (2015), cementing Earth Rocker as a key chapter in Clutch’s evolution.
